name: Ligaya Mishan
beat: NYC-focused restaurant criticism, with some national reach
note: NYT dropped critic anonymity with this appointment, so her identity is public; NYT also adds brief starred reviews from other writers.
ratingSystem: NYT stars, 0 to 4, plus Critic's Pick. Gave only two four-star reviews so far (Yamada, Albi). Also writes the NYT 100 Best list.
howTheyDine: Face is public since June 2025. Books under aliases; the Times pays. Up to three visits per restaurant. Sat with her back to the room in low light on her first assignment.
caresAbout: Imagination, ambience, service, technique, passion and deliciousness. Loves immigrant-run and hole-in-the-wall places. Judges a place for what it is, not against fine dining.
recognizeBy: Public face; appears in NYT videos. May sit with her back to the room.
whyItMatters: Her stars are the most important review in New York.
relevanceToIara: High. NYC-based and drawn to immigrant cooking. No Brazilian review by her found.

recentReviews.verdict: Four stars. First NYT four stars outside NYC.
Two stars, Critic's Pick. Praised heat used as one flavor among many.
Four stars for its kaiseki menu.

name: Tejal Rao
beat: Nationwide restaurant criticism; California-based, travels often
note: Former NYT California critic (since 2018), James Beard award winner; no longer anonymous.
ratingSystem: NYT stars, 0 to 4, plus Critic's Pick. Reviews nationwide.
howTheyDine: Based in California and travels to review. Face public since June 2025. Books under aliases; the Times pays. Says perfect anonymity was never realistic.
recognizeBy: Public face; appears in NYT videos.
whyItMatters: Same NYT stars as Mishan, but mostly outside NYC.
relevanceToIara: Low to medium. Mishan covers NYC; Rao covers the rest of the country.
caresAbout: Small places and overlooked workers. Sharp on fine dining. Will give a $3 bread as much attention as a tasting menu.

recentReviews.verdict: Two stars, Critic's Pick. Called the tiny spot one that goes big.
Two stars. Lively, clear vision of modern Black diaspora food.
Three stars for the revival by Emeril's son.

name: Matthew Schneier
role: Chief restaurant critic (took over from Adam Platt, Aug 2023)
note: Former fashion/culture writer (The Cut, NYT) turned critic; reviews run on Grub Street.

photoCredit.text: Cultured magazine interview, cross-checked with Cultured group portrait

caresAbout: Value, not price. Judges a place by its own ambitions. Picks hyped, high-profile openings and mixes price points.
whyItMatters: One of the last full-time critics in America. Drives downtown buzz.
relevanceToIara: High. Reviewed a South American grill (Graciela) favorably and covers new Manhattan openings.
ratingSystem: No stars. New York magazine paused its rating scale; reviews are prose. Also writes short First Taste pieces and best-of lists.
howTheyDine: Books under assumed names or has friends book. Several visits on different days, hours and group sizes. Skips disguises.
recognizeBy: No published tells. His face is not hidden.

recentReviews.verdict: Win for Argentina; maybe the best new steakhouse in NYC.
Positive. The sequel to Noortwyck fans the fire.
Overcurated and underwhelming.

name: Helen Rosner
role: Food correspondent / staff writer; writes the Tables for Two restaurant column (took over from Hannah Goldfield by Sept 2025)
note: Won the 2024 James Beard Craig Claiborne Distinguished Criticism Award; ex-Eater and Saveur editor.
ratingSystem: No stars. Weekly review column The Food Scene, which won a 2024 James Beard Award.
whyItMatters: Three-time James Beard winner; big national readership.
relevanceToIara: Medium. Reviewed a South American fire restaurant soon after opening.
howTheyDine: First visit is a normal meal with a non-food friend she likes, to judge the vibe. Little research before going.
caresAbout: Feel and vibe first, then the food. Will pan a big name: she said she could not recommend La Boca.
recognizeBy: Usually dines with a friend who is not in food. No other published tells.

recentReviews.verdict: Very bad. All smoke, no fire. Visited days after it opened.

name: Hannah Goldfield
role: Staff writer; former Tables for Two critic (first full-time New Yorker restaurant critic, 2018)
note: Stepped down from the Tables for Two column; Helen Rosner now writes it. Exact step-down date not verified.
whyItMatters: 2024 James Beard winner. No departure from the New Yorker found; still listed as staff writer.
ratingSystem: No stars. Writes for Tables for Two.
caresAbout: Drinking culture, mini cocktails, no-alcohol options (2026 interview).
relevanceToIara: Medium. Covers NYC restaurants and bars.

name: Gwendal Poullennec
role: International Director of the MICHELIN Guides
beat: Oversees all Guide selections worldwide, including North America
note: The Guide's public face; inspectors themselves are anonymous. 2026 Northeast Cities ceremony (incl. NYC) is Dec 14 at the Glasshouse, Manhattan.

name: Michelin Guide inspectors (anonymous)
note: Book under assumed names and pay in full; cannot be identified by face or name. Treat every table equally.
ratingSystem: Stars (1 to 3) and Bib Gourmand. Stars need inspector agreement.
howTheyDine: Anonymous, assumed names, no notes at the table, pay in full. Often solo; in pairs at couples places. May reveal themselves only after paying.
caresAbout: Ingredient quality, technique, harmony of flavors, the chef's personality, consistency across visits.
recognizeBy: No reliable tells. A solo diner who orders widely and pays, then asks to talk, may be one.
whyItMatters: Stars or a Bib Gourmand change a restaurant's fate.
relevanceToIara: High. Consistency every night is what they test.

recentReviews.verdict: New one stars: Bridges, Huso, Muku, Yamada.

name: Elazar Sontag
beat: National-profile critic based in DC; former Bon Appetit restaurant editor
note: Publicly shows his face and restored star ratings; still avoids reserving under his own name. Could visit NYC.
ratingSystem: Brought back WaPo stars in Dec 2025. One star means good. Highest is four (Izakaya Seki). Counter spots can earn top stars.
howTheyDine: Not anonymous. Always books under aliases and pays his own way. About eight meals a week. Multiple visits.
caresAbout: Whether a place is the best, most consistent version of itself. Broad taste: Lao, Ethiopian, Vietnamese.
recognizeBy: Public face. Former Bon Appetit restaurant editor.
whyItMatters: Ran Bon Appetit's Best New Restaurants list; national taste-maker.

recentReviews.verdict: Four stars, his first.

name: Pete Wells
role: Reporter covering food (former chief restaurant critic, 2012 to Aug 2024)
note: Kept his face out of print for his whole run as critic, so there is no reliable photo. Booked under fake names.
ratingSystem: Gave NYT stars 2011 to 2024. Gave Brazilian Botequim two stars in 2014.
howTheyDine: Fake names; a friend checks in first. Three visits, each with three friends. Waited two months after opening. Did not send food back.
whyItMatters: Stepped down Aug 2024; still at the Times.
relevanceToIara: Low now. Shows NYT critics value good Brazilian food.
recognizeBy: Arrives after his party. Nonprescription glasses. Lots of food, little alcohol. Fingers flutter near temples. Studies each dish.

recentReviews.verdict: Two stars. Great feijoada and suckling pig; basement location hurt it.

name: Florence Fabricant
role: Food and wine writer; Off the Menu column on new openings
beat: New restaurant openings and food news
note: Her Off the Menu column is where NYC openings get announced.
whyItMatters: Off the Menu is where NYT readers learn about openings.
ratingSystem: No ratings. Writes the weekly Off the Menu (openings) and Front Burner columns.
relevanceToIara: High for PR. A listing there announces a new restaurant.

name: Eric Asimov
note: Likely to notice the wine program as much as the food.
whyItMatters: Sets the tone on wine lists and pricing.
ratingSystem: No restaurant ratings. Chief wine critic since 2004; writes The Pour weekly.
caresAbout: Wine with food. Critical of high restaurant wine prices. Prefers good wine over trophy wine.
relevanceToIara: Low. Know the wine list and fair pricing.

name: Priya Krishna
role: Food staff reporter; interim restaurant critic from July 2024
note: Filled in as critic alongside Melissa Clark after Wells. Whether she still reviews after June 2025 is unverified.
ratingSystem: Gave NYT stars as interim co-critic from Aug 2024 into 2025. Now a reporter and video host.
howTheyDine: Wore wigs and costumes as a critic. Brings comedians as companions. Takes leftovers home.
caresAbout: South Asian and immigrant food; no waste.
recognizeBy: May wear a wig. Takes leftovers home.
relevanceToIara: Medium. Covers food culture stories, not starred reviews now.

name: Sam Sifton
role: Assistant managing editor; founder of NYT Cooking, former food editor
note: Influences NYT food coverage decisions. Exact 2026 portfolio unverified.

name: Ryan Sutton
outlet: The New York Times / The Lo Times
role: NYT contributing critic (since Nov 2025); runs The Lo Times
note: NYT contributing critic since Nov 2025; also runs The Lo Times newsletter.
recognizeBy: Face public since Nov 2025. Pays by Apple Pay, so no name on the card.
caresAbout: Prices and value. Steak, sandwiches, tacos. Whether the food justifies the spend.
whyItMatters: Now gives NYT stars. Former Eater NY chief critic.
relevanceToIara: High. Covers new NYC spots and Latin American grills; picanha fits his beat.
ratingSystem: NYT contributing critic since Nov 2025: short starred reviews in the Where to Eat newsletter. No formal scale on The Lo Times.
howTheyDine: Showed his face in Nov 2025. Still books under pseudonyms and pays with Apple Pay so his name never shows.

recentReviews.verdict: One star (good).
Praised the $33 ox steak.
Reviewed its beef rib fingers; wrote on Latin American steakhouses.

name: Robert Sietsema
role: Independent writer; laid off from Eater Dec 2024, started Substack in 2025
beat: Cheap eats and neighborhood NYC dining
note: Decades-long NYC dining chronicler (ex-Village Voice, Eater) who writes about LES-type neighborhood places.
recognizeBy: Hides his face in photos (a devil mask, a camera). Treat any regular solo diner taking notes seriously.
caresAbout: Cheap immigrant food made by people cooking from home. Value. New openings across all boroughs.
whyItMatters: 35+ years covering NYC; reviews new spots fast.
relevanceToIara: High. Writes early reviews of new downtown openings.
ratingSystem: No stars. Paid Substack, three posts a week. Early reviews, lists, cheap eats.

recentReviews.verdict: Review of the reopened Midtown deli.
Memorable ribs and sausage; great potential.
Early review of a new global Indian spot.

note: Reviewed NYC for New York magazine for 22 years before Matthew Schneier took over; not currently reviewing.

role: Former NY Daily News restaurant critic and food editor; active podcaster in 2026
note: Longtime radio/podcast voice, still publishing 2026 episodes.

name: Keith Lee

note: About 17M TikTok followers (May 2025); his visits create the 'Keith Lee effect' and he says he pays and has family pick up to avoid VIP treatment.

recognizeBy: Very famous face; millions of followers.
whyItMatters: One video can fill a room overnight. Hosted a 10,000-person NYC food festival in May 2025.
relevanceToIara: Medium. NYC picks so far are casual spots.

caresAbout: Crust, sauce, cheese, vibe. Leans New York thin crust.
recognizeBy: Famous face; usually a camera crew.
relevanceToIara: Low. iara does not serve pizza.
